data_collection.description: Customer transaction and demographic data may be unbalanced, leading to biased sampling that underrepresents certain groups.
data_collection.mitigation: Conduct a demographic distribution audit and rebalance the dataset using targeted sampling or synthetic augmentation to ensure all groups are proportionally represented.

data_collection.description: Sensitive demographic attributes may be collected without explicit user consent, raising privacy and ethical concerns.
data_collection.mitigation: Implement clear consent documentation and restrict data collection to fields essential for model performance; communicate data usage transparently to users.

modeling.description: Model predictions may systematically favor majority customer groups due to historical bias embedded in training data.
modeling.mitigation: Apply fairness-aware training methods, including reweighting, bias constraints, and evaluation across demographic slices before finalizing the model.

modeling.description: Complex model architecture may produce opaque predictions that stakeholders cannot interpret or challenge.
modeling.mitigation: Use interpretable models where possible or integrate explainability tools (e.g., SHAP values) to provide reason codes for predictions.

deployment.description: Model drift may cause degradation in prediction fairness as customer behavior changes over time.
deployment.mitigation: Implement continuous monitoring pipelines that track fairness metrics and trigger alerts when deviations exceed thresholds.

deployment.description: Lack of human oversight during automated recommendations may lead to unreviewed harmful decisions.
deployment.mitigation: Introduce human-in-the-loop review for high-impact decisions and maintain audit logs for all automated outputs.
